interpretations: Join each budget line to its matching event, discarding unmatched lines. Group the joined lines by `event_name` and compute `AVG(budget.amount)`, ignoring NULL amounts. Compute the overall average as the unweighted average of those per-name averages. Return only names whose average is strictly above the overall average, with their per-name average, their average minus the overall average, and their average divided by the unweighted average of the returned names’ averages. Do not round
queries:
WITH per_name AS (
    SELECT e.event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS name_avg
    FROM budget AS b
    JOIN event AS e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event
    GROUP BY e.event_name
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(name_avg) AS overall_avg
    FROM per_name
),
returned AS (
    SELECT p.event_name, p.name_avg, p.name_avg - o.overall_avg AS difference
    FROM per_name AS p
    CROSS JOIN overall AS o
    WHERE p.name_avg > o.overall_avg
)
SELECT
    event_name,
    name_avg,
    difference,
    name_avg / (SELECT AVG(name_avg) FROM returned)
FROM returned
